description: WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the extended '9x' arm of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:162-168, reached from 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE at :138-150 - the third of that paragraph's three call sites and the one no abending OPEN or READ case in this folder reaches; case19 is the folder's other close failure and reaches it over three fixture rows where this case reaches it over one. case08, case09, case10 and case16 reach 9910 from the OPEN at :120-132 and case12, case13, case17 and case20 reach it from the READ at :93-113, so between the three the shared paragraph is proved shared at every call site rather than incidentally right at one (gate G47). THE RUN, statement by statement: :121 answers '00' so the open succeeds; the loop at :74-81 reads the single seeded row and :78 DISPLAYs it; the next READ at :93 reports '10', so :99 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT, 88 APPL-AOK at :104 is false, 88 APPL-EOF at :107 is true and :108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE, which ends the loop; :83 then PERFORMs 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, where :137 ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT sets the assumed-failure value, the CLOSE at :138 fails, :139 takes its ELSE, :142 ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT sets twelve, 88 APPL-AOK at :144 is false, and :147-150 run in order: DISPLAY 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE', MOVE CARDFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. Five lines and RETURN-CODE 12, with TIMING 0 at :156 and ABCODE 999 at :157. THERE IS NO 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C' LINE: :85 sits after the PERFORM at :83 and CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :158 does not return, so the closing banner is lost even though the record line emitted before it stands. That interaction is what only a close failure can state - the four abending OPEN cases display no record at all, and the five abending READ cases lose the banner from a different paragraph - and it is the reason the arm is worth pinning here rather than only at unit level. THE REDEFINES, WHICH THIS ARM IS THE ONLY USER OF (gate G34): :53-56 declare 01 TWO-BYTES-BINARY PIC 9(4) BINARY and 01 TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES TWO-BYTES-BINARY with 05 TWO-BYTES-LEFT PIC X and 05 TWO-BYTES-RIGHT PIC X. It is CBACT02C's only REDEFINES and :164-167 is the only place it is used: two typed accessors over one backing span, written through the alphanumeric view and read back through the numeric one, which is how the paragraph converts a byte into an integer. :164 MOVE IO-STAT1 TO IO-STATUS-04(1:1) passes the first status byte through verbatim; :165 MOVE 0 TO TWO-BYTES-BINARY zeroes the halfword; :166 MOVE IO-STAT2 TO TWO-BYTES-RIGHT deposits the second status byte into its low-order byte through the redefinition, so the field then holds that byte's unsigned value; :167 MOVE TWO-BYTES-BINARY TO IO-STATUS-0403 renders it into a PIC 999 as three zero-filled digits, which never truncates because the maximum is 255. IO-STATUS-04 is four characters - IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 plus IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at :57-59 - the literal at :168 is twenty, so the emitted line is twenty-four; every width counted from source (practice B11). THE STATUS AND ITS IMAGE, DERIVED: a CLOSE that fails has no two-character equivalent to report, so it is reported under COBOL's own '9' permanent-error convention - '9' followed by a feedback byte - which is precisely the case :162-163 tests for before rendering. The reachable feedback byte is BINARY ZERO: AccountBalanceReaderJob.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS is '9' followed by X'00', and its own declaration records why the byte is zero rather than invented, namely that a translated data-access failure carries no VSAM feedback code to report. For that status the deciding operand of the OR at :162-163 is the FIRST one, IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC: X'00' is not a digit, so the class condition holds and the arm is taken before IO-STAT1 is examined at all. Step :166 then deposits X'00', step :167 renders 000, and :168 displays the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' immediately followed by the image 9000, which is FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000 in twenty-four characters. The trailing NNNN of the literal is emitted verbatim and is not a placeholder the image replaces (practice B5). THE CODE PAGE, NAMED, BECAUSE THIS ARM CONVERTS A CHARACTER INTO DIGITS (practice B8): whenever the feedback byte is printable the three digits move with the encoding, so the code page has to be named rather than assumed. ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET names US-ASCII explicitly, and application-test.yml together with config/CobolCharsetConfig expose only the two keys IBM037 and US-ASCII, so US-ASCII governs here. Binary zero is X'00' in both code pages, which is exactly why THIS case's 000 is the one value of this arm that does not move with the encoding - stated rather than left looking like a coincidence. The encoding-dependent form of the same arm is a status of '90', whose second byte is the character '0': common/FileStatus.toStatusImage was read and renders it 9048, because '0' is 0x30 = 48 under US-ASCII, three digits 048, image 9048; under IBM037 the same character occupies 0xF0 = 240, and a mainframe reading EBCDIC would display 9240 instead. That form also fires the OTHER operand of :162-163, since '90' IS numeric and IO-STAT1 = '9' is then what decides it. It is not asserted here because AccountBalanceReaderJob cannot produce it: CardReadResult reports a CICS response, FileStatus.batchStatusOfCicsResp translates only NORMAL, ENDFILE, NOTFND, DUPREC and DUPKEY, and every other response falls to PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS, so '9' followed by X'00' is the only extended status this job can ever hand the renderer. Fabricating 9048 here would mean fabricating a feedback byte no backend reported, which is the one thing PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS exists not to do, and it would also be a line no production constant emits. The value is pinned where it is genuine instead: FileStatusTest drives the renderer directly with '90' expecting 9048 and walks the raw second byte to 0x0A giving 9010 and 0xFF giving 9255, FileStatusSemanticsTest repeats the '90' assertion, and CBACT03C/case16 pins it at parity level because the cross-reference repository does carry a two-character status. Recorded here rather than absorbed silently (practice B4). THE ROW, AND WHY IT IS THIS ROW: one inline row whose FILLER X(59) carries the twelve characters 00000001940 closed by '}'. CVACT02Y declares no signed field at all, so the FILLER is the only span of a card record whose content the copybook does not constrain - a span that holds no field, that CBACT02C never writes, and that READ ... INTO CARD-RECORD at :93 fills with whatever the row held. Those twelve characters are a genuine PIC S9(10)V99 image: eleven leading digits and a trailing '}', which carries both the sign and the low-order digit, so the twelve digits are 000000019400 and the value is -194.00 at scale 2. They are row 1 of acctdata.txt's ACCT-CURR-BAL image with the sign inverted, which is the field this program's Java class name gestures at and never touches. The expectation is that the DISPLAY line equals the seeded row exactly: rendering the line from the six decoded fields would agree on all six and emit fifty-nine spaces for the FILLER, destroying the overpunch and with it the value it denotes, and trimming the row or reading the trailing byte as a bare sign rather than as a digit and a sign does the same damage. Carrying that row on the case whose CLOSE then fails is deliberate: one run proves the byte-for-byte pass-through, the record line that stands, and the banner that is lost, and the FILLER assertion stays on a case where a record is actually emitted. INPUTS AND OUTPUTS: inputs holds the row verbatim at its declared 150 bytes under the CARDFILE binding key and never a dataset name (gate G46), and no normalisation is declared because carddata.txt's rows are already the width CVACT02Y declares. jobParameters is empty because app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare EXEC PGM= with no PARM and CBACT02C has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into. expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty and that is an assertion, not an omission: :120 opens CARDFILE INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE, so the job whose prompt-mandated name says AccountBalanceReader reads the CARD file and writes nothing whatsoever (AAP rule R1, divergence register 0.8.4). THE INJECTED CONDITION IS NAMED IN THIS PROSE because ParityCase offers a batch case no other channel: forcedOutcomes belongs to ParityCase.ScreenRequest and a BATCH_JOB case is refused a screenRequest outright, so this case names the call site - the CLOSE at :138, after the open answered '00' and the loop reached end of file - and parity/CBACT02CParityTest arranges it as Scenario.closeFailing(), exactly as case08 through case16 have their shapes arranged there. PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here was DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl and app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt and against the renderer in common/FileStatus; nothing was captured from a running COBOL program, because none can be run in this environment - AAP 0.7.6 lists eight independently verified blockers and 0.9.11 escalates the substitution as risk R-A. Only the provenance of the expected values changes: the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the zero-diff gate all stand.
